speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's heading to Japan.
zh: 是的，它正前往日本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going quite fast, actually.
zh: 它实际上走得相当快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so it travels around 17,000 miles an hour.
zh: 是的，所以它每小时大约绕行 17,000 英里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about an hour and a half to do one circumnavigation.
zh: 完成一次绕地球航行大约需要一个半小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I mean, by StarCloud 4 or so, this won't be like one.
zh: 所以，我是说，到了 StarCloud 4 左右，这不会像是一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll be a giant network sort of covering the Earth, actually.
zh: 它实际上将是一个覆盖地球的巨型网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, from StarCloud 3 onwards, we'll have 88,000, and they'll all fly.
zh: 是的，从 StarCloud 3 开始，我们将有 88,000 个，它们都会飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one is in what they call mid-inclination orbit, so it doesn't go over the poles.
zh: 这一个处于他们所谓的中倾角轨道，所以它不经过两极。

speaker: Unknown
en: StarCloud, and that's another point here on how janky this one is.
zh: StarCloud，这也是关于这一个有多简陋的另一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't even fly in the right orbit, but at least it enables us to test the hardware.
zh: 它甚至不在正确的轨道上飞行，但至少它让我们能够测试硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next one will fly over the poles, and that gives us 24-hour always in the sun.
zh: 下一个将飞越两极，这给我们 24 小时总是在阳光下。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to do that, do you need to put thrusters on the satellite to move it into that orbit?
zh: 为了做到这一点，你需要在卫星上安装推进器将它移入那个轨道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the end, they will be deployed in that orbit, but you need thrusters anyway to maintain the orbit because you have drag from the upper atmosphere there.
zh: 最后，它们将被部署在那个轨道中，但无论如何你需要推进器来维持轨道，因为你有来自那里高层大气的阻力。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the engineering and physics trade-offs you have to make this happen?
zh: 你必须做出什么样的工程和物理权衡才能实现这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because what you basically are doing with StarCloud is you're getting infinite energy because the sun is basically the natural fusion reactors, just a giant mass that...
zh: 因为你在 StarCloud 上基本上做的就是你获得了无限的能量，因为太阳基本上是天然的聚变反应堆，只是一个巨大的质量体……

speaker: Unknown
en: generates a nuclear reaction with the giant mass, and you have infinite energy, basically abundant, and lots of space.
zh: 通过巨大的质量产生核反应，而且你有无限的能量，基本上是丰富的，和大量的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a result of that, which we're constrained of that in Earth, you have a bunch of other really hard problems to solve, like things around interconnect, how do you send all the data back and forth back to Earth?
zh: 但正因为那个结果，也就是我们在地球上受到的那种限制，你有一堆其他非常难的问题要解决，比如关于互连的事情，你如何把所有数据来回传回地球？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you handle cooling?
zh: 你如何处理散热？

speaker: Unknown
en: People think that space is cold, but actually there's no, unlike Earth, there's no air to circulate it back.
zh: 人们认为太空是冷的，但实际上没有，不像地球，没有空气来循环它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need some crazy solutions with...
zh: 所以你需要一些疯狂的解决方案，用……

speaker: Unknown
en: cooling.
zh: 散热。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's things around radiation to flip the bits in processors.
zh: 还有一些关于辐射导致处理器中比特翻转的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's probably other things around how to get the solar panels to become really big and expand.
zh: 可能还有其他关于如何让太阳能电池板变得非常大并展开的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many more.
zh: 还有更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, these are the ones that I could think of.
zh: 我的意思是，这些是我能想到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's like so many things that are just so hard to build.
zh: 我的意思是，有太多事情真的很难构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you are correct.
zh: 是的，你是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many engineering challenges to be solved.
zh: 有许多工程挑战需要解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: The two biggest ones that are outstanding and most of our engineering team is split basically 50-50 down these two lines is number one, as you mentioned, how do you get rid of this heat in a vacuum?
zh: 两个最大的悬而未决的问题，我们的大部分工程团队基本上是按这两条线 50-50 分配的，第一，正如你所提到的，如何在真空中排掉这些热量？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then number two, how do we make the chips work in a higher radiation environment?
zh: 然后第二，我们如何让芯片在更高辐射的环境中工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the other problems are being solved by other people.
zh: 其他一些问题正在由其他人解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: The interconnect, we've just signed a contract with SpaceX for our next 20 satellites to have a Starlink laser terminal.
zh: 关于互连，我们刚与 SpaceX 签了一份合同，为我们的下 20 颗卫星配备 Starlink 激光终端。

speaker: Unknown
en: That gives us very high bandwidth, low latency connectivity.
zh: 这给了我们非常高的带宽、低延迟的连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other people are solving some other parts of this.
zh: 其他人正在解决这个问题的一些其他部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The core ones we're solving are that.
zh: 我们解决的核心问题是那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for the first one, for the thermal management side of things,
zh: 所以对于第一个，对于热管理方面的事情，

speaker: Unknown
en: We are building a very large, low-cost and low-mass deployable radiator.
zh: 我们正在构建一个非常大的、低成本和轻质量的可展开散热器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, radiators in space are not new.
zh: 现在，太空中的散热器并不是新鲜事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not a new physics solution.
zh: 这不是一个新的物理解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more of a manufacturing and engineering challenge because the International Space Station has had a radiator which dissipates lots of heat already.
zh: 这更多是一个制造和工程挑战，因为国际空间站已经有一个可以散掉大量热的散热器了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very similar mechanism, so a liquid-cooled loop.
zh: 非常相似的机制，也就是液冷回路。

speaker: Unknown
en: The challenge with it is making it cheap and light.
zh: 其中的挑战是让它变得便宜和轻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our radiator is at least 10 times less mass per watt of dissipation than the ISS radiator.
zh: 所以我们的散热器每瓦散热的重量至少比国际空间站的散热器少 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: and 500 times less cost per watt of dissipation than the ISS radiator.
zh: 每瓦散热的成本比国际空间站的散热器少 500 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So very easy benchmark to beat on cost for the ISS.
zh: 所以在成本上，要打败国际空间站的标准很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on radiation, it's just a lot of ground testing in different particle accelerators.
zh: 然后在辐射方面，就是在不同的粒子加速器中进行大量的地面测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've done several rounds of testing at the Brookhaven National Lab particle accelerator for heavy ions.
zh: 所以我们已经在布鲁克海文国家实验室的粒子加速器进行了几轮重离子测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also there's a cyclotron for high-velocity protons down in Knoxville.
zh: 另外在诺克斯维尔有一个回旋加速器用于高速质子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we ship all of our hardware down there.
zh: 所以我们要把所有的硬件运到那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: My co-founder Addy runs in and out wearing this protective thing.
zh: 我的联合创始人 Addy 穿着那个防护服跑进跑出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Addy is a lunatic when it comes to this stuff.
zh: Addy 在这方面是个疯子。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, oh, yes, it's the same as flying transatlantic.
zh: 他就像，哦是的，这就像飞越大西洋一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't worry about the radiation.
zh: 别担心辐射。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, basically you expose it over a 24-hour period to the same radiation dose that you would have in a five-year mission.
zh: 所以，是的，基本上你会在 24 小时内暴露它，接受相当于五年任务期间的辐射剂量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all of that telemetry and data then informs our choice on both shielding and software to mitigate bit flips.
zh: 然后所有这些遥测和数据会告知我们在屏蔽和软件方面的选择，以缓解比特翻转。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're the only people in the world now that know where both an H-100, a B-200, H-200 will fail if you blast it with high velocity protons and heavy irons.
zh: 我想我们是现在世界上唯一知道 H-100、B-200、H-200 在哪里会失效的人，如果你用高速质子和重离子轰击它们的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have to change any of the underlying electronics to solve the problem or you just build shielding around it?
zh: 你需要更改任何底层电子设备来解决这个问题吗，还是你只是在它周围构建屏蔽？

speaker: Unknown
en: Both, both.
zh: 两者都有，两者都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do build shielding around it.
zh: 所以我们确实在它周围构建了屏蔽。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of it is just component selection.
zh: 很多时候这只是组件选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, all of the SSDs, all of the power delivery system, all of the power converters and everything else, we test 10 components and whichever the best one is, we pick.
zh: 所以，例如，所有的 SSD，所有的供电系统，所有的电源转换器和其他所有东西，我们测试 10 个组件，哪个最好，我们就选哪个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying not to use space-grade, rad-hard components.
zh: 我们试图不使用太空级、抗辐射组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to use off-the-shelf, like automotive-style components because it's way cheaper.
zh: 我们试图使用现成的，像汽车级组件，因为它们要便宜得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most people have never tested those in radiation chambers.
zh: 大多数人从未在辐射室中测试过这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's one of the secrets of how SpaceX has actually reduced a lot of the costs of a lot of the satellites as well.
zh: 我认为这也是 SpaceX 实际上降低许多卫星成本的秘诀之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: They use not space-graded electronics, which would be exorbitantly very expensive, but instead you take regular components that there's a supply chain and run through all the tests and make sure if it works.
zh: 他们不使用会非常昂贵的太空级电子设备，而是采用有供应链的常规组件，并通过所有测试确保它能工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think actually this is one of the things that Stranis...
zh: 而且我认为实际上这也是 Stranis……

speaker: Unknown
en: does as well, to make sure that telecommunication satellites actually work in space.
zh: 所做的事情之一，以确保通信卫星真正在太空中工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they're also in GEO, which has more radiation.
zh: 因为它们也在 GEO，那里的辐射更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you in GEO as well?
zh: 你们也在 GEO 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, we're in LEO.
zh: 不，我们在 LEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you first told people that you were going to put data centers in space, what were people's reactions?
zh: 当你第一次告诉人们你要在太空部署数据中心时，人们的反应是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: For a very long time, their reactions was, this is the dumbest thing I've ever heard.
zh: 在很长一段时间里，他们的反应是，这是我听过的最愚蠢的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually applied to YC once and we got rejected.
zh: 所以我们实际上申请过一次 YC，然后被拒绝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We then tried to raise, and we tried to raise $2 million at 10 posts on a safe.
zh: 然后我们试图融资，我们试图以 1000 万美元的估值融资 200 万美元，基于 SAFE。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took us three months and we got rejected from at least 100 VCs.
zh: 我们花了三个月时间，被至少 100 家 VC 拒绝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then even after YC, when we went out to raise after demo day, I think we got rejected from at least 20 VCs before we got to the first check.
zh: 甚至在 YC 之后，当我们在演示日之后出去融资时，我想我们在拿到第一张支票之前被至少 20 家 VC 拒绝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's one of these ideas that was extremely unpopular with investors.
zh: 这是一个在投资者那里非常不受欢迎的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you had listened to what all the investors were telling you, you would have quit and not ever done this idea.
zh: 如果你听了所有投资者告诉你的话，你就会退出，永远不会做这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, why did people tell you that they were not investing and what did they get wrong?
zh: 我很好奇，为什么人们告诉你不投资，他们哪里弄错了？

speaker: Unknown
en: people had a hard time visualizing a world with low cost launch.
zh: 人们很难想象一个低成本发射的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be fair, we're still not out of the woods on that front.
zh: 公平地说，我们在那个方面还没有完全脱离困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, lots of things need to go right with the Starship program for that to make sense.
zh: 你知道，Starship 计划需要很多事情顺利推进，这才有意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one thing.
zh: 所以这是第一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it just sounds too sci-fi and too...
zh: 我认为这听起来太科幻了，太……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, to make this work, there's a convergence of two factors.
zh: 是的，为了让这行得通，有两个因素需要汇聚。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the launch costs coming down, and people have to believe that.
zh: 一个是发射成本下降，人们必须相信这一点。 [[221] ] 第二个是，在陆地上建造东西变得难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is it becoming way harder to build stuff terrestrially.
zh: 第二是，在地面建设基础设施正变得极其困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe two years ago, that wasn't quite as obvious as it is today.
zh: 也许两年前，这还不像今天这样明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now people are like, okay, well, they've just banned building new data centers in New York.
zh: 现在人们会说，好吧，他们刚刚禁止在纽约建立新数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to ban it in like seven other states.
zh: 他们将在大约其他七个州禁止它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those two things, I think, converge to make it more investable, essentially.
zh: 我认为这两件事的汇聚，使得它本质上更具可投资性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the other thing, after hearing you explain all the engineering and physics, it actually is doable.
zh: 我认为另一件事是，在听完你解释所有的工程和物理学之后，这实际上是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't sound like sci-fi from first principles.
zh: 从第一性原理来看，这听起来并不像科幻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually buildable.
zh: 它实际上是可建造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason I had confidence in it is because we had such a strong engineering team.
zh: 我对此有信心的原因是因为我们有一个非常强大的工程团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you have the world's best space engineers saying this is possible, and to be frank, my background isn't as a space engineer.
zh: 所以如果你有世界上最好的太空工程师说这是可能的，坦率地说，我的背景不是太空工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, I have full confidence in my two co-founders, one from SpaceX, the other was building satellites for NASA, saying it's possible then, you know.
zh: 但是，你知道，我对我的两位联合创始人充满信心，一位来自 SpaceX，另一位在为 NASA 建造卫星，他们说这是可能的，那么，你知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: that's a it's a it's good enough for me once you had the idea and then once you're in yc how did you sort of break the problem down into like a plan for what to do obviously in software it's you think of your mvp and you launch quickly and you get feedback but hard to do that with data centers in space i have a very tangible piece of advice for all space companies the first thing every space company should do is book the first available launch they can
zh: 那对我来说这就够了。一旦你有了这个想法，一旦你进入了 YC，你是如何把这个问题分解成一个计划的，关于要做什么，显然在软件领域，你会考虑你的 MVP，你快速发布并获得反馈，但对于太空中的数据中心很难做到这一点，我对所有太空公司有一个非常具体的建议，每个太空公司应该做的第一件事就是预订他们能预订的最早的发射。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before they built the thing that they're going to launch.
zh: 在他们建造他们要发射的东西之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before they built the thing.
zh: 在他们建造那个东西之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before they probably even know what they're going to launch.
zh: 甚至在他们可能甚至不知道他们要发射什么之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Booking a launch is such a good forcing function for a space company.
zh: 预订发射对太空公司来说是一个非常好的强制函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we founded the company January 1st, 2024.
zh: 所以我们于 2024 年 1 月 1 日创立了公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: January 2nd, we booked the first available SpaceX rideshare launch.
zh: 1 月 2 日，我们预订了第一次可用的 SpaceX 拼车发射。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was cheap.
zh: 而且很便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like 300 grand.
zh: 大概是 30 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which was how far out was the launch?
zh: 发射排期是多久以后？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was 18 months out, and then it got pushed to 21 months out.
zh: 是 18 个月后，然后它被推到了 21 个月后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were like, okay, something is going to be on that rocket.
zh: 我们当时想，好吧，那个火箭上会装上一些东西的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not 100% sure what it's going to be at this point, but something is going to be on there.
zh: 我现在不是 100% 确定那会是什么，但会有东西在那上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's interesting.
zh: 这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sounds like the same advice for all the software companies.
zh: 听起来像是给所有软件公司的同样的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've just got to keep launching and launching.
zh: 你得不断地发布和发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same thing.
zh: 同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we initially planned to launch was very unimpressive, actually.
zh: 而我们要推出的最初计划其实非常不起眼。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like we were going to put a Jetson chip, which has been flown on many satellites before, and we were going to use it for kind of edge processing and things.
zh: 就像是我们要放一个 Jetson 芯片，这东西已经在很多卫星上用过，我们要用它来做边缘处理之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually had a co-founder change quite early on when we got Addy from SpaceX.
zh: 我们其实在很早的时候经历了一次联合创始人变更，那时我们招来了 SpaceX 的 Addy。

speaker: Unknown
en: Addy was like, oh, that's lame.
zh: Addy 就说，哦，那太逊了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, let's put an H100 on there.
zh: 就像是，把 H100 放上去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're like, Addy, you can't put H100 on a satellite.
zh: 我们就说，Addy，你不能把 H100 放到卫星上。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like...
zh: 他说……

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure you can.
zh: 当然可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: The amount of people who said it was physically impossible to run a chip that's that power dense in orbit.
zh: 有很多人说，在轨道上运行功率密度这么高的芯片在物理上是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: People just thought it was literally impossible to run data center grade GPUs on orbit.
zh: 人们就认为在轨道上运行数据中心级 GPU 根本是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would have caused it to be impossible?
zh: 是什么会导致它变得不可能呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two things.
zh: 有两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the thermal side of things.
zh: 一个是热力学方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're very power dense.
zh: 它们的功率密度很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: They produce a lot of heat.
zh: 它们产生很多热量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second is they've never been tested in the radiation environment or space.
zh: 第二个是它们从未在辐射环境或太空中测试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And both of those...
zh: 而这两方面……

speaker: Unknown
en: So for the first one, it's kind of a wacky solution.
zh: 所以对于第一点，这是一个有点古怪的解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: We submerged the entire thing in this phase change material.
zh: 我们把整个东西浸没在这种相变材料中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything on StarCloud 1 is submerged in this phase change material.

en: what was it like to have this idea have people sort of poo-poo it like didn't really get it and then suddenly i mean to have much more commercial validation that like you know google um spacex the the stalwarts of the industry sort of embrace the idea and realize actually like some crazy percentage of future data centers likely are going to be in space what was that like to sort of see the the sea change and be early
zh: 有这样一个想法，人们有点看不起它，不太理解它，然后突然间，我是说，有了更多的商业验证，比如你知道，谷歌，SpaceX，行业的中流砥柱，某种程度上接受这个想法，并意识到实际上，未来数据中心很大一部分可能会在太空中，看到这种海啸般的变化并处于领先地位，那是什么感觉？

en: It was surreal.
zh: 这感觉超现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you go back through my Twitter feed, I've been like shouting from the rooftops for the last like three years about this.
zh: 如果你翻看我的 Twitter，过去三年我一直在像在屋顶上大喊一样宣传这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Contrarian, but right.
zh: 逆向而行，但是是正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day I would post something about like why datasets in space are going to make sense.
zh: 每天我都会发一些关于为什么太空中的数据集会有意义的东西。

en: And then slowly and slowly and slowly, people would start to drop hints about things.
zh: 然后一点一点地，人们开始开始暗示一些事情。

en: Like Elon at one point was like...

zh: 所以我会转发那个并说，我们需要在太空建设数据中心。

en: Like everything I would find a hook for.
zh: 就像我找到的所有东西我都能找到一个挂钩。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is one of the things we see with all the best hard tech founders.
zh: 我认为这是我们在所有优秀的硬科技创始人身上看到的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're essentially living in the future and are almost like a prophet that brings the future back to now us underlings and the earth that don't quite get it yet.
zh: 你基本上生活在未来，几乎像一个先知，把未来带回到现在的我们这些还不明白的下属和地球上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to tell my mom, who's very religious, that YC said I'm a prophet.
zh: 我要告诉我妈妈，她很虔诚，YC 说我是个先知。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that's cool.
zh: 但我认为这很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing that's fascinating to me is that your background, if you go on your LinkedIn, it's not very legible that you would be in space.
zh: 另一个让我着迷的事情是，你的背景，如果你看你的领英，并不是很明显你会从事太空行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you had a background previously doing software and physics and then went to business, but nothing there that sets space.
zh: 但是你之前有软件和物理学的背景，然后去了商学院，但那里没有任何设定是太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: yeah um so for people who don't know my background um spent the first five years of my career as a an engineer on the software side studying math and physics before that um undergrad and masters and then i went to mckinsey more on the commercial product side but i actually ended up doing a couple of projects with national space agencies on different satellite missions and that's where i really started to notice the launch costs coming down very rapidly
zh: 是的，所以对于不了解我背景的人，我在职业生涯的前五年是一名软件方面的工程师，在此之前学习数学和物理，本科和硕士，然后我去了麦肯锡，更多是在商业产品方面，但我实际上最终为不同的国家太空机构做了一些卫星任务项目，那是我真正开始注意到发射成本非常迅速下降的地方

speaker: Unknown
en: actually had another uh startup before this um and yeah when i left that one decided okay if i'm going to do another startup it has to be something i'm like very passionate about and and yeah for my whole life i've been very passionate about space because i don't have a space engineering background realized okay i'm gonna need

zh: 世界上最棒的太空工程师，实际上这归功于 YC，我有点盲目地遵循 YC 的建议，我想，好吧，在提出想法之前我们需要做的第一件事就是把世界上最不可思议的太空工程师基本上招入团队

en: This was before you even knew what you wanted to do in space.
zh: 那是在你甚至知道你想在太空做什么之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: All you knew at that point was that like launch costs were going to come down dramatically and there was going to be cool stuff to do in space.
zh: 在那个点你知道的全部就是发射成本会大幅下降，而且在太空会有很酷的事情可以做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you wanted to find some space people to do it with.
zh: 你想找一些太空人一起做这件事。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 是的，字面上的。

zh: 但这不是那种，哦，你能请建设我有的这个疯狂想法吗的氛围。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the reverse even.
zh: 甚至反过来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I'm going to figure out the commercial part.
zh: 就像我要弄清楚商业部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，确切地。

en: My pitch to Adi and Ezra was essentially, if you have any ideas that would make sense if the launch cost was 10x less than it is today, I can figure out everything else around that besides building the satellite piece.
zh: 我对 Adi 和 Ezra 的推销基本上是，如果你有任何想法，如果发射成本比今天低 10 倍就会讲得通，除了建设卫星部分，我可以弄清楚周围的所有其他事情。

en: How did you find them?

en: How did you recruit them?

en: Actually, to be frank, I messaged a lot of space engineers.
zh: 实际上，坦白说，我给很多太空工程师发了信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe 10 of them took a call and two of them said yes.
zh: 大概 10 个接了电话，2 个答应了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's all you need.
zh: 这就是你所需要的。

en: You don't need like 100 people to do it.
zh: 你不需要 100 个人来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You only need one or two.

en: So Philip, during the batch...

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you will.
zh: 我认为你会的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's occurred to me since then that it's not actually clear to me anymore that that is necessary for StarCloud to succeed.
zh: 但从那时起我意识到，对我来说 StarCloud 成功并不一定需要那样清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious if you think about it the same way, because since the batch, we've learned that AI data centers are becoming politically incredibly unpopular.
zh: 我很好奇你是否以同样的方式思考，因为从那批以来，我们了解到 AI 数据中心在政治上变得非常不受欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seems not unlikely to me that it will soon become basically de facto impossible to build AI data centers anywhere, at least in a democratically-hyped country.
zh: 在我看来，这似乎并非不可能，很快就会变得基本上事实上不可能在任何地方建设 AI 数据中心，至少在一个民主炒作的国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious how you think about that, how it affects your plans for the company.
zh: 我很好奇你是怎么想的，这会如何影响你对公司的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, 100%.
zh: 是的，百分之百。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this has moved faster than I was expecting as well, to be honest.
zh: 老实说，这实际上也比我预期的进展要快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've just seen New York now blocking data centers construction.
zh: 我们刚刚看到纽约现在正在阻止数据中心的建设。

en: For reasons which are not grounded in science, really, it seems more like vibes than anything else.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a lot of misconceptions about certainly water and data centers, but also power.
zh: 关于水与数据中心，当然还有电力，确实有很多误解。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the things that come to your mind?
zh: 你想到了哪些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: With water specifically, water is really actually just a function of power.
zh: 具体谈到水，水实际上真的只是电力的一个函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can cool data centers with no daily consumptive use of water if you just throw more power at the problem, essentially.
zh: 如果你基本上把更多的电力投入到这个问题上，你可以在没有日常消耗性用水的情况下冷却数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is what all of the data center companies are now proposing.
zh: 这就是现在所有的数据中心公司都在提议的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very unlikely that any data center company proposes any data center that is going to be consuming daily amounts of water.
zh: 任何数据中心公司提议任何会消耗日常水量的数据中心都是不太可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is actually evidence that you can have closed-loop systems that consume very little water.
zh: 实际上确实有证据表明，你可以拥有消耗极少水的闭环系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the analogy is like if you ran a burger shop, a fairly large data center with hundreds of megawatts would consume about the same amount of water as a McDonald's.
zh: 我认为这就好比如果你经营一家汉堡店，一个拥有数百兆瓦的相当大的数据中心消耗的水量大约和一家麦当劳一样多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really a non-issue, but it's unbelievable that they're repeating this so much.
zh: 所以这真的不是问题，但他们如此频繁地重复这一点简直令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do use a lot of power, though.
zh: 不过，它们确实消耗大量的电力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so most new power projects for data centers right now are being built with natural gas generators, actually.
zh: 因此，目前大多数为数据中心新建的电力项目实际上都是使用天然气发电机建造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's certainly some people that are pushing back on those.
zh: 当然也有些人对此表示反对。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the arguments is that as data centers get built, they sort of compete on the grid, which is kind of not true.
zh: 其中的一个论点是，随着数据中心的建成，它们在电网上竞争，这有点不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also not true if you build a new power project for it.
zh: 如果你为此建立一个新的电力项目，这也是不成立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, which is generally what people are doing.
zh: 对的，这通常是人们正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just can't get enough power from the grid.
zh: 你只是无法从电网获得足够的电力。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also some evidence, actually...
zh: 实际上也有一些证据……

speaker: Unknown
en: that adding data centers increases the capacity of the grid and then prices actually come down over time.
zh: 添加数据中心增加了电网的容量，然后价格实际上随着时间的推移而下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: That being said, it's sort of a perfect storm.
zh: 话虽如此，这有点像一场完美风暴。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need intelligence.
zh: 我们需要智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need data centers.
zh: 我们需要数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's become basically a national security issue.
zh: 这基本上已成为一个国家安全问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: For America and for the West to have access to intelligence is sort of the most important tech tree of the next hundred years.
zh: 对于美国和西方来说，能够获得智能是未来一百年的科技树中最重要的一环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for tech policy to sort of put us back into the Stone Age and possibly lose the war for us, that puts StarCloud in a different position in terms of bringing compute and AI and power online.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, for sure.
zh: 是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: It definitely puts us squarely in the national security bucket at that point.
zh: 在这一点上，这确实将我们牢牢地置于国家安全的范畴内。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, thank you so much for fighting for the West then.
zh: 我的意思是，非常感谢你为西方而战。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're doing our best.
zh: 我们正在尽我们所能。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you learned and what would you tell the just starting out version of yourself based on where you're at now?
zh: 你学到了什么，基于你现在所处的位置，你会对刚开始的自己说什么？

en: Yeah, I mean, I think there's just huge opportunities now coming in with space.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为随着太空时代的到来，现在正迎来巨大的机遇。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're really at the very early innings with what's going to be this enormous industry in space.
zh: 我们真的正处于这个将成为太空巨大产业的早期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: The amount of capacity and launch that's going to come online in the next five years is really mind-boggling.
zh: 未来五年将上线的容量和发射数量真的令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I would definitely encourage people to step into that.
zh: 所以是的，我绝对鼓励人们踏入这个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of advice, the YC advice stands true.
zh: 就建议而言，YC 的建议依然是真理。

en: It's technical talent on the founding team is the thing you need to solve for first, and then everything else follows from there.
zh: 创始团队中的技术人才是你首先需要解决的问题，然后其他一切都随之而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Philip, thanks so much for coming on The Light Cone.
zh: Philip，非常感谢你做客 The Light Cone。

en: Yeah, thanks so much, Alan.

en: Nice being here.
